title: FAUST. V. Hot methanol in the [BHB2007] 11 protobinary system; hot corino versus shock origin
question: What are the physical properties, spatial origin, and desorption mechanism (hot corino thermal desorption versus accretion shock) of hot methanol in the [BHB2007] 11 protobinary system?

recipe.goal: Reconstruct continuum maps, extract radial profiles, and compute continuum SED and spectral indices for disk and envelope
recipe.method: Reconstruct continuum maps across the three setups with a common 0.35 arcsec clean beam, extract radial brightness profiles in elliptical annuli (PA = 167 deg), measure disk fluxes via 2D Gaussian fits (or closed contours at 15, 120, 230 sigma) and envelope fluxes via contours (>5 sigma excluding the disk), and perform a linear fit in log-log scale to compute the SED spectral index.
key_parameters: Common clean beam = 0.35 arcsec; elliptical annuli PA = 167 deg East of North; disk closed contours at 15, 120, 230 x rms (setups 3, 1, 2); envelope contour > 5 x rms

recipe.goal: Create moment maps, extract spectra, identify molecular transitions, and fit Gaussian velocity components
recipe.method: Create integrated intensity (moment 0) and velocity field (moment 1) maps for methanol lines using 12-m data; extract average spectra over the >4 sigma polygon of the 218.440 GHz moment 0 map; identify transitions using CASSIS linked to CDMS/JPL databases; fit 3 Gaussian velocity components (-2.0, 2.8, 9.9 km/s) using Levenberg-Marquardt fitting in CASSIS; fit 2D Gaussians to channel maps using CASA imfit to measure deconvolved component sizes.
key_parameters: Polygon extraction threshold > 4 sigma in integrated intensity map; 3 velocity components at V_LSR = -2.0, 2.8, and 9.9 km/s

recipe.goal: Estimate beam-averaged methanol column density and rotational temperature via LTE Rotational Diagram analysis
recipe.method: Construct rotational diagrams in CASSIS for each of the three velocity components from the integrated intensities extracted in the 4-sigma polygon of the 218.440 GHz transition, excluding the blended 261.7 GHz component at -2 km/s, and fit a straight line (order 1 polynomial) accounting for rms and 10% calibration uncertainty.
assumptions: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE), optically thin emission, beam-filling factor of 1 (beam-averaged)

recipe.goal: Derive gas kinetic temperature, H2 volume density, methanol column density, and source size via non-LTE LVG radiative transfer modelling
recipe.method: Model the 12C and 13C methanol transitions up to J=15 simultaneously for each of the three velocity components using the LVG code grelvg over a grid of ~10000 models, minimizing chi^2 over N(CH3OH), n_H2, T, and source size theta_s.
key_parameters: Transitions up to J=15 (7 CH3OH transitions + 1 13CH3OH transition); Linewidths = 3.2 km/s (-2 km/s comp), 6 km/s (2.8 km/s comp), 5 km/s (9.9 km/s comp); Grid: N(CH3OH) = 1e13 to 2e18 cm^-2, n_H2 = 1e5 to 1e9 cm^-3, T = 15 to 200 K (~10000 models)
assumptions: Spherical geometry; A-/E- CH3OH ratio = 1; 12C/13C = 68; para-H2 collisional coefficients from Rabli & Flower (2010)

recipe.goal: Estimate foreground dust optical depth and line attenuation towards 11A and 11B
recipe.method: Invert the Planck flux density equation using 225 GHz continuum flux densities and deconvolved source sizes from Alves et al. (2019) to compute dust optical depth tau_nu over a grid of dust temperatures T_d from 100 to 500 K.
key_parameters: T_d = 100 to 500 K (steps of 10 K from 100-200 K, 20 K from 200-500 K); nu = 225 GHz
assumptions: Distance d = 163 +/- 5 pc; solid angle Omega_s ~ A/d^2

recipe.goal: Determine spatial and kinematic origin of the three methanol velocity components via PV diagram and 2D Gaussian channel centroid fitting
recipe.method: Extract a position-velocity (PV) diagram along the velocity gradient (PA = 140 deg, width = 0.5 arcsec) for the 243.916 GHz line; create moment 0 and 1 maps over three velocity intervals ([-7, 0], [0, 6], [6, 16] km/s); fit 2D Gaussians to each velocity channel of the 243.916 GHz line to measure peak centroids and compare with 11A, 11B, and high-velocity CO centroids.
key_parameters: PV cut PA = 140 deg East of North, width = 0.5 arcsec; centroid selection thresholds: peak > 5 x Gaussian fit error and SNR > 10.0 (accuracy < 0.02 arcsec)
assumptions: Emission in each velocity channel is compact and centrally peaked; positional accuracy is Theta / (2 x SNR)

However, exact imaging parameters (tclean settings, cell/image size, self-cal solints), continuum rms values, polygon vertices, and the grelvg code itself are not provided.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA Large Program 2018.1.01205.L data are public in the archive, the target and spectral lines are unambiguously specified, and the main quantitative results (continuum spectral indices, 3-component Gaussian line fits, LTE rotational temperatures/column densities, non-LTE LVG parameters, and 2D channel centroids) are tabularly reported and can be reproduced from the visibility data.
